title: money as creative practice

changing your relationship to money is not a 10 step checklist, it's tending to an ongoing practice -- with curiosity and tenderness -- as you do with your creative work. I'll share my own personal stories and significant reframes -- ⁠money as a circle⁠, as feminine force, as a ⁠child of your creative energy⁠.

I'll walk you through my 7 practices for working with money -- and invite you to see money as a portal for working with your sense of resourcedness, enoughness, worthiness to receive, and your power to claim what you desire.

In the last episode, we finished the mini-series by centering on your art as the sun of your universe, the life source that fuels everything else. Today, I am excited to talk about what feels like the antithesis, but is actually very much a part of the same energetic space, and that is your relationship with money.

I think talking about money can feel really hard and triggering even thinking about it. In this episode, I want to explore how we relate to money with the same tenderness and curiosity as we do our creative practices, our bodies, our bodies of work, our digital worlds, with the same quality of attention and intention.

Money is Not Linear

And the first thing to acknowledge is that the process of working with money is not linear. It's not a 10-step checklist you can execute and be done with. Just like you never feel done with your creative work, with making art, the ways in which we relate to money changes throughout our lives as our needs and desires change.

And if we think about creative energy as an intangible resource that we receive through inspiration, through practice, and we give through creating things and putting it out into the world, then we can think of money as the material parallel of how we receive and channel our creative resources to offer something to the world.

Money is a puzzle that I've spent much of my career obsessing over, and part of it was because I felt so triggered by the phrase "monetizing your passion." Somehow it just felt so extractive and so linear and killed my sense of passion for whatever I was doing. And so I had to recreate, reimagine, entire money paradigm to make it feel okay for me to even look at money.

Three Essential Principles

The three essential principles I'll share with you today is that one, money is an ongoing relationship. You can nurture it and tend to it the way you do every other relationship.

And two, money is not a linear result or outcome of something. Money is a part of a circle. Any money I receive from a client or course, it came from an idea an intention, a vision, that is the seed of this circle. And the circle continues by me flowing my creative resources, my time, into what I create and then receiving resources for what I create, taking that energy and investing it back into my ecosystem.

So when you look at your income and expenses, that's just one data point on that circle. The seed of that started with an intention, a vision, nourished by your practice and process that you put into this work.

When money is a part of a circle, it makes it feel more fluid, malleable, organic. I can enter the circle from many points on it. It's no longer the harshness of a accounting spreadsheet. It's a warm place by the campfire. And I can approach it, relate to it in many different ways.

The third principle is that creative energy is the mother of money. I wrote a post about this a couple of years ago. This is about being clear about what the power dynamic is. Creative energy is not competing for money in your life. It is the life source that animates the circle of money, that creates your offerings, that birthes money through what it creates and what it desires.

Seven Practices

Because I relate to everything in my world through immersion and practice and process, I want to apply the same practices to money work. I know that this money work is essential for the future that I want to build. How can I make it feel safe to take care of this relationship with money in a way that doesn't feel like obligation, it doesn't feel heavy? How do I create a gentle ongoing rhythm, much like tending to my digital world or writing my newsletter, that I'm willing to sit down with on a regular basis?

My answer to this is creating seven practices that are nonlinear and modular, as in you can enter the circle from any point of the practice. These practices are the foundation on which I'm teaching a new course called money juice cleanse. Each practice will be distilled into the container of a juice box. You can pick it up and put it down one sip at a time.

To give you a bit of personal context, I have avoided money and saw money as the enemy for many many years. And when I first started working for myself, I spent a lot of years grappling with money shame because I grew up in a frugal Chinese immigrant family. Money is such a loaded topic culturally. It carries such a heavy weight of making your parents proud, being a good daughter, living up to their expectations and dreams in this new country.

Many years ago, a friend said to me, "Money is just a number that makes me feel things." And I think back to that sentence all the time because money makes me feel a lot of things. These feelings are channels for doing deep transformative work.

In this episode, I won't go into business infrastructure or ecosystems, but I will talk about money as energy, money as creative practice, as spiritual work, as a portal to relating to your sense of self-worth and worthiness, feelings of power or powerlessness, responsibility, expectations, freedom, agency, what we owe our communities and families versus what we owe ourselves, our personal desires, needs, and wants.

Practice 1: Clarity

So let's dive in to practice one, clarity, facing the numbers.

The first obstacle or resistance to work with in doing money work or money play, shall we say, is to literally show up to face the numbers. Facing the numbers is not about scrutinizing every single transaction and making a super detailed budget, but it is about creating enough clarity in your mind that can help clear this faint background static that is your money anxiety.

I find that the more that I avoid the numbers, the more this background anxiety builds. Avoidance keeps me in the murky territory of not needing to confront anything, therefore not needing to take responsibility, and just living in a vague place of, "I hope it will work out, but I'm worried that it won't," which is not a place of our power.

I think to be in our power with relates to money is to know exactly with clarity what we need to do now and what we are focusing and channeling our energy to make happen in the future.

And if the word financial reality feels triggering, let me provide this reframe. Reality can feel like hitting a concrete brick wall, but reality is just what exists in the present moment. It's just a snapshot. It's not an indictment of what's going to happen tomorrow. What happens in the future is always fluid, and even the present moment reality changes when you look at it from different lenses.

Working for yourself, having a business is really scary, and it's also magical because the reality of tomorrow is you could have a new opportunity, make money unexpectedly from many directions.

So the practice of clarity is grounding in what you currently have in this moment and looking at the different streams of inflow and outflow, looking at your needs and desires for the future. And the way you do this is not through a complicated budgeting spreadsheet, but creating a simple, safe ritual that makes it feel easy, gentle, and soothing to do this work in 10 minutes on a regular basis.

How can you create a money ritual around clarity and treat it like a creative practice? Maybe you begin with a cup of tea, an affirmation that it is safe to be here, and to move through the numbers with a sense of purpose.

The practice of clarity is an acquired taste. It's something that gets easier the more that you do it because as you find more clarity, you build the muscle of self-trust in meeting yourself wherever you are.

Practicing clarity is like getting a longitude and latitude of your current location. That makes it possible to move from here into the future, which is unknown and mysterious. When you know where you are, then you can support yourself in what you need and create an intention to move forwards.

Practice 2: Embodied Safety

The second practice is embodied safety.

I think of embodied safety in two ways. The first is in the practical things that support you, whether that's a day job or savings or income streams that pay the bills or support from your family or a partner. It's different elements in your ecosystem that create a sense of safety like a net that you can fall back on.

And maybe this net doesn't feel like it's serving the next evolution of you. Maybe you want to take a leap and change your entire business or leave your job. And the question here is what is the right dosage of risk taking that feels comfortable enough for you to not trigger you into total scarcity freefall mode, but is uncomfortable enough to stretch you where you need to grow one step at a time.

And the answer to that question is very different for each of us and can change over time. When thinking about practicing embodied safety, I would encourage you to ask your nervous system how much risk it's willing to handle as you look at the practical elements or income streams that are currently supporting your life and creating that sense of safety before you decide to evolve them or let them go.

The second part of creating embodied safety is that safety is a feeling. Even if you have enough money, enough runway to last you a year or three years, you can still feel the anxiety of not having enough. Safety is a relative feeling and the goalpost can always be moving.

In a recent workshop I taught inside labyrinth called embodied abundance. I use the metaphor of a cup. When we feel that we have enough, the cup is full, but if there's a hole at the bottom, then no matter how much more money we receive, we will never feel totally safe.

So what do we do? We look at the cup, the container itself, which is your body, your psyche, your emotional landscape, and practice the feeling of safety.

When you feel safe in your body, then you allow your nervous system to rest. You're able to let go of the sense of hypervigilance, to not feel like you're constantly being chased by a tiger, that if you take a day off or a week off, nothing bad will happen. You allow yourself to rest, rest as a way of replenishing your energetic resources.

When you feel resourced because you feel safe, you're able to make decisions in your life and in your business, not from a place of fear or lack, but from a place of curiosity and desire.

And the practice here is somatic. It's asking yourself what allows you to feel embodied safety in the here and now. How is embodied safety a sensation that you can tune into in just a few minutes by centering in your body? Is there an affirmation you can say to anchor in that feeling?

Practice 3: Detoxing Old Stories

Practice three is detoxing old stories. So this is the hard work of deprogramming and rewriting narratives that play in the back of our heads subconsciously.

I will give you a couple of examples.

It was very hard for me to choose my artistic path over the expectations of my family and cultural upbringing. And I was extremely rebellious and aware of the weight of the shame that I carried. So at the beginning of my journey, I believed that I needed to reject money in spite of all of this shame, because if I wanted to be a real artist, I needed to be poor and I was willing to be poor. And of course, this rejection of money blocked money for me.

The belief that I've since rewritten and reprogrammed myself to embody is to carry my work, my art as a channel for abundance, to say out loud that artists can be rich. They deserve to be rich, to take our money and our creative resources and to do good things in the world to take care of communities and the world.

The second story that I worked through is to see money as a man that I hated needing. So money became part of this power relationship dynamics, this kind of patriarchal father figure. I hated the fact that I needed money to exist in this world.

In the last many years, I have reframed money to see money not as a masculine energy, but as a feminine force. Money to me is like the empress in tarot. It is a manifestation of my creative abundance. It comes to me with ease and pleasure and joy. It's a reflection of my inner creative magic. And so this gendered reframing of money transformed it from something that I resisted, rebelled against and fought against into a nurturing force of nature that I allow myself to cultivate and receive.

A third example of an old story is the triangle of productivity, self-worth and money. This is the belief that how productive you are on a given day or week or year is directly related to your sense of self-worth. And the more productive you are, the more money you could make.

This is dis-tangling these three things from each other, that how much money you make is separate from your sense of self-worth and how productive you are doesn't necessarily co-relate to how much money you receive, nor is it a reflection of how worthy you are.

Because to subscribe to this triangle of productivity, self-worth and money is to believe that in order to be worthy, we need to be constantly producing and being "productive." And that is the capitalist narrative that we are taking a radical departure from.

It is so hard to imagine and believe that something different is possible without first examining these old narratives. The work here, the practice of detoxing, is shining a light on background stories, exposing them, looking in the closet of your psyche, the back rooms of your inner programming, because awareness is more than half the work.

And as you operate on a day-to-day basis, you will catch yourself. Where does this anxiety come from? Why am I not letting myself rest? What is the belief that is motivating me right now?

When you catch yourself with these old stories, you can consciously work to release them by rewriting new beliefs which will feel uncomfortable at first, and then it will feel like second nature. And of course, like all the other practices, this is not a one-time thing. It's something you return to again and again.

Practice 4: Gratitude

Practice four is gratitude. That's bringing attention and intention to what you already have, your current resources.

Resources are fluid and changing, and a lot of them are intangible. It's not just your material wealth or possessions. It's also the resource of your energy, your attention, your time, your mind, your experience, your skills, your essence, your passion.

When someone absorbs your work, they're giving you your resources. Even if they're not paying you money, they're giving you a moment of their life. And so this practice is about acknowledging what you already have. When we give things attention, we feed it in our imagination. We're attending to it in our minds.

I think the practice of gratitude can sound really cheesy and fake positivity. So the way that I think about it is calling in my resources from the atmosphere.

Because money is a part of a circle, when you realize how much you have, you're willing to share it. You're willing to give it with generosity. And when you give it, when you share it with the world, it will come back one way or another.

My personal practice for working with gratitude is to write an affirmation that starts with thank you universe. And I name what it is that I have in my life, the gifts that life has given me, whether it's my body, my community, my relationships, my deep feelings, my life experiences. And I state that I would like to offer this back to the world. I say out loud that I allow life, spirit to move through me as if I am a channel for beauty and truth and creation.

I don't know exactly how this works, but when I'm really clear with this practice, synchronicities will happen in my life unexpectedly. I will get some kind of signal within a couple of days, whether that's an inquiry from a new client or selling a course or just some unexpected gift that drops into my lap.

I'm very hesitant about the quote unquote manifestation magic that a lot of spiritual gurus talk about, but I will say that the energetics of gratitude do create its own magnetic force. The more that you acknowledge what it is that you have as a gift from life, the more that life seems to give you gifts.

Practice 5: Receiving

Practice five is receiving. This is worthiness and desire work.

I think one way that people talk about worthiness is to use the dilemma of pricing. Pricing is a number that makes us feel things. Do we deserve to be paid this much? Do they feel like they're getting enough value? Am I worthy of this? Am I worthy to receive good things in my life? New projects, new opportunities, money, is my work enough?

My personal story is that as a child, I always felt like I needed to overperform. And a lot of it was the Asian American immigrant child competition, that kind of environment that I grew up in. I felt like I needed to make an effort to be exceptional just to feel like I was enough.

And so as an adult in my business, I have to catch myself when I have the anxiety of, "Did I give enough?" The impulse to over-deliver comes from a deeply rooted place where there's work I can do.

And the question is, if you did nothing other than exist, what do you feel worthy of? Do you feel like you need to earn it? How can you work with your nervous system, with your body, with your energetic container? That when you receive good things, when a client pays you or someone buys from you, can you hold the satisfaction of that?

This practice could be useful if for you giving doesn't feel hard, receiving is what feels hard.

And the second part of that work is claiming your desire because money without a container or a purpose is meaningless. So it's just substituting for a sense of safety that we actually desire. So what do you desire? Be more specific than just more money. What will you do with that money? How much do you need? Do you feel like you deserve it? Do you feel worthy of it? What beliefs or stories are blocking the sense of worthiness?

When I work with what it is that I desire and I work with the sources of friction and resistance that are blocking me subconsciously, I dig out the old stories that believe somehow I don't deserve it.

I kid you not, very mysteriously, life always leads me to what I desire within a span of days or weeks. And again, this is not saying the magical words of manifesting something. It's about energetic clarity, creating these open channels for receiving that which we want and calling that in.

If we think of ourselves as radio towers, then we have to be clear about what the signal is that we want and to work with what has been blocking or creating static in that signal.

Practice 6: Circulation

Practice number six is circulation.

Generally speaking in my money work, I don't use the word income or expenses. Even when I'm doing taxes for myself, I prefer to use the words inflow and outflow because whatever I spend as outflow is a channeling of my resources and whatever comes into my world as inflow is a result of creative outflow, weeks and months and years of nurturing my ecosystem.

So the practice of circulation is allowing yourself to be inflow with life, with the world through the channel of your work. It's like your work is the bridge between your personal experience of life of this world with what you offer others, companions on this journey, people you can serve and guide, people who share the same values and passions as you do. Your work is a channel that allows you to be in conversation with life and money is one byproduct of that channel.

So the practice of circulation is combining practices four and five of gratitude and receiving. It's looking at what do I have, what resources are available to me, where is my abundance located? As an example for me, I feel an abundance of deep feelings and imagination and empathy and poetry and ideas. I feel an abundance of relationships and to practice circulation is looking at my abundance and asking myself what can I share? What can I give generously without expectation of anything in return? And to do that through the practice of my work, through making the work, sharing the work.

And the last part is opening my palms to receive, allowing myself to feel safe receiving, being clear about what it is that I desire to receive.

Circulation is about flow. There are many moments in my career when someone gave me a gift of some sort. And when I asked if I could pay them back, they would say, "You don't have to give back to the same source that you received from. You can pass it on." That wisdom stayed with me.

The practice of circulation is walking through the world with my hands open and my heart open. It's cultivating my resources so that I can give them away, which requires a deep sense of embodied safety, trusting that you are enough and you have more than enough to share.

Practice 7: Abundance

Practice number seven is abundance as a cosmic spiritual practice.

I mentioned earlier that the feeling of enoughness is when your cup is full. The feeling of abundance is not a number quantifiable amount. It's a felt sense. What feels like scarcity to one person can feel like abundance to another.

I mentioned earlier that enoughness is like having a cup that is full. In that metaphor, abundance is having a cup that is constantly overflowing. And the feeling of abundance is very foreign to our systems because capitalism is built on scarcity.

But like the feeling of embodied safety, I like to work with abundance by starting in the body in the felt sensations. And this can feel hard at first, which is why it's practice number seven. If you don't relate to the feeling of abundance, if your body seems to find it unsafe or difficult, then start with feeling enough. Work with feelings of enoughness up to abundance as of increasing a dosage.

Abundance, enoughness, all of that is relative. You could be a millionaire and still feel scarcity. Abundance isn't about hoarding possessions or money in the bank. It's about being a channel for infinite resources. And that's why I think of it as a deeply spiritual practice, connecting to the cosmic atmosphere of creative abundance, of life source, of spirit.

I think of my creative energy as a part of this cosmic flow. It comes from a source that is out there. I'm always standing in the stream of abundance and allowing myself to be a channel through which abundance flows through and moves on. I would keep myself as an open node.

The practice here starts again with tuning into the body. What would it feel like to move, live, create from a deep felt sense of your own abundance? What if you knew that you could satisfy all of your needs and desires for your life, that you have the infinite resources to do so, that they will come to you when the time is right? What would it feel like to soak in your own abundance relative to your creative life, your personal life, your relationships?

The feeling of abundance is a process and it's a practice that we can return to every day.

closing

Today I shared seven non-linear modular practices for nurturing your deep relationship with money. I invite you to return to these again and again like peeling back layers of the onion.

The first is clarity to face the numbers. The second is embodied safety, trusting that you are safe in the here and now. The third is detoxing old stories and releasing old programming. The fourth is gratitude, appreciating your resources. The fifth is receiving, believing in your worthiness and claiming what you desire. The sixth is circulation, opening channels for inflow and outflow. And the seventh is abundance, connecting to the cosmos and life.

My journey in grappling, working with, and transforming my relationship with money is exactly what I talked about in the last episode about letting my artist child grow up and infuse her energy, her voice, her perspective into the material world to become a sovereign leader.

In this way, you can see your relationship to money as a channel for relating to your creative energy, your inherent worthiness, your sense of creative power, and as a resource and direct vein to claiming that which you desire, to nurturing your community, to taking care of micro and macro worlds, and to be in generative flow with life.

If you'd like to work with me to deepen these practices, you can join me for the live session of Money Juice Cleanse starting on Monday, where I will distill each practice into an audio teaching, a juice box illustration, prompts, resources, templates, and step-by-step practice guidance.

In a couple of weeks, I will also release Money Juice Cleanse as individual juice boxes, which you can explore in my apothecary.

If you'd like to read more about my writings and stories around money, there's a link to a curated page called Money Stories. If you'd like to do business infrastructure work, you can explore my business class called Digital Abundance.

The best way to keep in touch with me is through my newsletter. As always, you can explore more of my work and writings on my web world.

Take care. Until soon.
